title: Verification process wrapper
description: Objective: turn the existing caller-supplied verifier observation contract into a real external-effect wrapper. Deliverable: a runner module that launches an exact verification recipe only after a one-use effect activation, in the sealed candidate workspace, with shell-free argv, bounded environment/output/time, cancellation and Windows process-tree cleanup, then feeds the observed bytes/exit into the existing production verifier-execution and evidence-receipt surfaces. NOT in scope: daemon persistence, provider/Claude launch, recipe authoring policy, or canary tests. Its real consumer is the Durable verification receipt dispatch task created in this breakdown. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/evidence/verifier-process.ts, verifier-process.js, verifier-process.test.ts, and packages/runner/src/surface/evidence-surface.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && a plain-Node @moe/runner root smoke.
definitionOfDone: An accepted sealed recipe executes by exact executable/argv/cwd with shell disabled only after a coherent one-use activation grant; stale recipe/input/grant facts refuse with exact production code and layer before any child starts.
The wrapper captures bounded stdout/stderr/exit/timing evidence and passes it to the existing production verifier-execution/receipt builders rather than reimplementing receipt authority.

Timeout, cancellation, spawn error, output overflow, and ambiguous exit produce distinct stable outcomes; UNKNOWN never becomes a passing receipt and every Windows child/process tree is awaited and reaped.
Duplicate delivery cannot execute the recipe twice: replay either adopts a registered run or refuses under the exact grant/lock code, proven with an invocation-count assertion.
@moe/runner root exposes the wrapper and type closure, a plain-Node smoke exercises it, and focused runner typecheck/tests exit 0.
taskRails: TDD every behavior change; every refusal test pins the exact stable reason code and refusing layer, and generated sweeps assert a positive case count.
Use only public package roots across package boundaries; no deep imports, test-owned authority, mock-backed acceptance, or optimistic UNKNOWN upgrades.
Keep production files focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; stage and commit only explicit owned paths.
This is an external-effect boundary: never invoke through a shell or accept a free-form command string.

implementationPlan.description: CONTRACT MODULE. Create packages/runner/src/evidence/verifier-process-contract.ts plus its one-line sibling verifier-process-contract.js (`export * from "./verifier-process-contract.ts";`). It holds NO spawning. Contents: frozen `VERIFIER_PROCESS_ERROR_CODES` = [VERIFIER_PROCESS_RECIPE_SEAL_INVALID, VERIFIER_PROCESS_INPUT_MANIFEST_STALE, VERIFIER_PROCESS_RUNTIME_UNPROVEN, VERIFIER_PROCESS_EXECUTABLE_UNSUPPORTED, VERIFIER_PROCESS_WORKSPACE_INVALID, VERIFIER_PROCESS_SPAWN_FAILED, VERIFIER_PROCESS_TIMED_OUT, VERIFIER_PROCESS_CANCELLED, VERIFIER_PROCESS_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW, VERIFIER_PROCESS_EXIT_AMBIGUOUS, VERIFIER_PROCESS_TREE_UNREAPED]; frozen `VERIFIER_PROCESS_LAYERS` = [LAUNCH_GATE, SPAWN, CAPTURE, REAP, REGISTRY]; `verifierProcessFailure(code, layer, message)` returning a frozen {ok:false, code, layer, message}; bounds `MAX_VERIFIER_OUTPUT_BYTES` (1 MiB per stream), `MAX_VERIFIER_RUN_MS`, `VERIFIER_REAP_GRACE_MS`; types `VerifierStreamCapture {bytes, byteLength, sha256, truncated}`, `VerifierCapture {stdout, stderr, exitCode, signal, startedAt, completedAt, durationMs}`, `VerifierClock {now(): string; monotonicMs(): number}`, and the refusal union `VerifierProcessRefusal` discriminated by `source: 'PROCESS' | 'SUPERVISOR' | 'EVIDENCE'` carrying respectively a VerifierProcessFailure, a SupervisorFailure verbatim, or an EvidenceFailure verbatim — foreign failures are NEVER re-coded, that pass-through is how the refusing layer stays readable. Also `hermeticVerifierEnvironment(base: NodeJS.ProcessEnv)`: allowlist SystemRoot, PATH, PATHEXT, COMSPEC, TEMP, TMP, USERPROFILE, HOME; force LC_ALL=C; drop everything else so no daemon secret reaches the child. `base` is a parameter — never read process.env here. Comment the WHY on the allowlist and on the source union only.
implementationPlan.note:
Contract module landed, no spawning in it. Frozen VERIFIER_PROCESS_ERROR_CODES (12) and VERIFIER_PROCESS_LAYERS (5). Deviation from the plan's literal code list, flagged in step-1: added VERIFIER_PROCESS_GRANT_RUN_DIVERGENT so the REGISTRY layer has a reachable code instead of being dead vocabulary (the grantId derives from intent+attempt only and never covers the recipe, so one grantId presented with two different recipes is a real collision). All 12 codes and all 5 layers will be swept for reachability in step 3.
Also added the three refusal constructors processRefusal/supervisorRefusal/evidenceRefusal next to the VerifierProcessRefusal union — the union alone would have forced the runner module to hand-build the wrapper object at ~12 sites, and a hand-built one is exactly where a foreign failure gets quietly re-coded. Foreign failures are carried verbatim.
hermeticVerifierEnvironment takes `base` as a parameter (never process.env), allowlists SystemRoot/PATH/PATHEXT/COMSPEC/TEMP/TMP/USERPROFILE/HOME case-insensitively because Windows env keys are case-insensitive, drops everything else, forces LC_ALL=C. One-line .js bridge added, matching the exact source runtime-entrypoint.test.ts's bridge guard requires.

implementationPlan.description: RED SUITE FIRST (TDD). Create packages/runner/src/evidence/verifier-process.test.ts against the not-yet-written `runVerifierProcess`; it must fail to resolve, and that is the starting state. Every refusal case asserts the EXACT code AND the refusing layer/source, never merely that it refused. Cases: (1) sealed recipe + coherent ActivationCommit + real Node launcher spawning `process.execPath -e 'process.stdout.write("ok")'` returns ok:true, disposition COMPLETED, exitCode 0, and `execution.argv` deep-equals `recipe.argv`; (2) same with `process.exit(3)` returns disposition FAILED, exitCode 3 — a proven failure still yields an admissible execution; (3) tampered recipe (mutated argv copy) refuses PROCESS/LAUNCH_GATE/VERIFIER_PROCESS_RECIPE_SEAL_INVALID with launcher invocation count 0; (4) input manifest whose sha256 no longer recomputes refuses VERIFIER_PROCESS_INPUT_MANIFEST_STALE, count 0; (5) grant already CONSUMED refuses source SUPERVISOR, layer GRANT, code GRANT_ALREADY_CONSUMED, count 0; (6) intent/attempt/grant that do not derive refuses source SUPERVISOR, layer ACTIVATION, code ACTIVATION_COMMIT_INCOHERENT, count 0; (7) runtimeObservation.truthClass UNKNOWN refuses PROCESS/LAUNCH_GATE/VERIFIER_PROCESS_RUNTIME_UNPROVEN, count 0 — and a sibling assertion that a PROVEN-but-non-recomputing observation is refused by source EVIDENCE at layer EXECUTION, proving the two layers are distinguishable; (8) argv[0] ending .cmd/.bat/.ps1 refuses VERIFIER_PROCESS_EXECUTABLE_UNSUPPORTED, count 0; (9) child that sleeps past the deadline refuses VERIFIER_PROCESS_TIMED_OUT and the capture is still returned; (10) pre-aborted and mid-run-aborted AbortSignal refuse VERIFIER_PROCESS_CANCELLED; (11) child writing more than MAX_VERIFIER_OUTPUT_BYTES refuses VERIFIER_PROCESS_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW with capture.stdout.truncated === true; (12) launcher whose close reports exit null and signal null refuses VERIFIER_PROCESS_EXIT_AMBIGUOUS and produces NO execution; (13) launcher whose close never fires refuses REAP/VERIFIER_PROCESS_TREE_UNREAPED; (14) launcher throwing ENOENT refuses SPAWN/VERIFIER_PROCESS_SPAWN_FAILED. Cases 1,2,3,8,9,10,11,14 use the REAL Node launcher; only 12 and 13 use a counting fake, because no real OS forces them deterministically. Add the closed-vocabulary sweep: collect the code from every refusal the suite produced into a Set, assert `set.size > 0` AND `set.size === VERIFIER_PROCESS_ERROR_CODES.length` — a code nobody can reach is dead vocabulary and this assertion is what stops it being added.

implementationPlan.description: MAKE IT GREEN. Create packages/runner/src/evidence/verifier-process.ts plus its one-line .js sibling. Exports: `ProcessLauncher` port (`launch(spec): LaunchedProcess` exposing pid, stdout/stderr chunk callbacks, a close promise, and kill()), the production `createNodeProcessLauncher()`, and `runVerifierProcess(input): Promise<RunVerifierProcessResult>`. Order is load-bearing and must read top-to-bottom as: GATE, then REGISTRY, then SPAWN. GATE (all before any child exists): `recipeSealMatches(recipe)`; input-manifest digest recomputes via `inputManifestDigestInput` and its baseIdentity matches; `validateActivationCommit(intent, attempt, grant)` COHERENT; `consumeActivationGrant(grant, wrapperIdentity)` CONSUMED; runtimeObservation.truthClass PROVEN; argv[0] extension not .cmd/.bat/.ps1; candidate cwd is a non-empty absolute path. REGISTRY: a module-level Map keyed by grant.grantId — an in-flight key ADOPTS by returning the identical promise so the launcher is invoked exactly once, a settled key REFUSES via the supervisor's `grantRefusal('GRANT_ALREADY_CONSUMED','GRANT',...)`; store only a settled marker, never captured bytes. SPAWN: `shell:false`, `windowsHide:true`, `stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe']`, cwd = sealed candidate root, env = `hermeticVerifierEnvironment(input.baseEnvironment)`, file = argv[0], args = argv.slice(1), and report `execution.argv` from the array actually handed to the launcher — never re-read from the recipe. CAPTURE: count bytes per chunk, cross MAX_VERIFIER_OUTPUT_BYTES -> kill tree + OUTPUT_OVERFLOW with truncated:true; resolve on close, NOT exit, so trailing bytes are not lost; digest each stream with `sha256Hex`. KILL/REAP: win32 `execFile('taskkill', ['/pid', String(pid), '/t', '/f'])`, posix `detached:true` + `process.kill(-pid,'SIGKILL')`; then AWAIT close within VERIFIER_REAP_GRACE_MS or refuse TREE_UNREAPED. Clear the deadline timer, remove the abort listener and detach stream listeners on EVERY exit path including refusals. CLASSIFY: exit 0 -> COMPLETED, exit non-zero -> FAILED, both then assembled into an `ObservedVerifierExecution` (timestamps from the injected `VerifierClock.now()`, duration from monotonicMs) and handed to the production `observedExecutionRejection(execution, recipe)` — if it refuses, return source EVIDENCE with its failure verbatim; only a null rejection yields ok:true. exit null and signal null, or a signal this wrapper did not send -> EXIT_AMBIGUOUS, no execution. Timeout -> TIMED_OUT, caller abort -> CANCELLED, both carrying the partial capture. Keep the file under 250 physical lines measured with `wc -l`; if it crosses, split the kill/reap helper out rather than trimming behaviour.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN except the root smoke, which is step 5's surface edit: 26 passed / 1 failed, the failure being exactly `ns.createNodeProcessLauncher is not a function` from the plain-Node probe. `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck` exits 0.
PER-FILE SPLIT (epic rail 5 is per FILE): one module would have been ~370 physical lines, so it is five, each well under 250 measured with `wc -l` (not Measure-Object): verifier-process.ts 97, verifier-process-run.ts 205, verifier-process-contract.ts 209, verifier-process-gate.ts 127, verifier-process-launcher.ts 94, verifier-process-capture.ts 49. This is a per-file split, not a task split. Every .ts has its exact one-line .js bridge; verifier-process.ts re-exports the launcher port and the input/result type closure so consumers still see one module.
Order is GATE (verifier-process-gate.ts) -> REGISTRY (verifier-process.ts) -> SPAWN/CAPTURE (verifier-process-run.ts). Gate order puts the abort check and the recipe/manifest integrity checks BEFORE consumeActivationGrant, so a refused launch never burns a one-use activation.
Registry: Map keyed by grant.grantId, entry is {recipeSha256, run}. The entry is inserted and `run` assigned entirely before the first await, so a same-tick duplicate adopts the identical promise and the launcher is invoked exactly once. On settle `run` is nulled — the entry survives as the one-use marker but holds no captured bytes.
Capture counts bytes AS CHUNKS ARRIVE and slices the tail at MAX_VERIFIER_OUTPUT_BYTES, so a chatty child cannot allocate before the check fires. Resolution is on 'close', not 'exit'. Kill is taskkill /t /f on win32 and process.kill(-pid) with detached:true on posix, and the wrapper then AWAITS close within the reap grace or refuses TREE_UNREAPED — kill is a request, reaping is the proof. clearTimeout and removeEventListener run in a finally, so they happen on refusal paths too.
UNKNOWN never becomes a pass: exit null with signal null, and a signal this wrapper did not send, both return VERIFIER_PROCESS_EXIT_AMBIGUOUS with no `execution` key at all. Only a null `observedExecutionRejection` yields ok:true, so the production evidence layer keeps final authority and an evidence refusal is returned verbatim as source EVIDENCE.

implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW — three real findings, all fixed before commit.
FIXED 1, argv read by ITERATOR. `const [file, ...args] = input.recipe.argv` destructures via Symbol.iterator, while recipeSealMatches (canonicalDigest) and observedExecutionRejection both read argv BY INDEX. A hostile Array subclass overriding Symbol.iterator would have spawned one command while the seal and the evidence layer inspected another. Replaced with readArgv(), an index-only single copy that is both spawned and reported, matching the discipline verifier-execution.ts documents in its own header.
FIXED 2, post-answer accumulation on the unreaped path. After TREE_UNREAPED the child is by definition still alive and still writing into a collector whose capture was already sealed. Added a `sealed` flag set in the same finally that clears the deadline; chunks arriving afterwards are dropped. Bounded before (the collector caps at 1 MiB) but it was retaining bytes nobody would ever read.
FIXED 3, honest limit undocumented. RUN_REGISTRY is process-lifetime, so it is the one-use memory for THIS wrapper and not across a restart; durable one-use memory is the daemon's compare-and-set. Written into the module header rather than left implied.
CHECKED AND SOUND, no change needed: a second same-grant call cannot reach the launcher twice (the entry and its promise are both installed before the first await, proven by an invocation-count assertion) and an adopted promise propagates a rejection to BOTH callers while `run.then(settle, settle)` keeps the settle path from becoming an unhandled rejection. Every timer is cleared and the abort listener removed in a finally, and awaitReap clears its own timer in its own finally, so the refusal paths clean up identically to the happy one. Overflow is counted per chunk with the tail sliced at the bound, never concatenate-then-measure. A killed tree uses taskkill /t on win32 and a process-group kill on posix, and a grandchild that escapes and holds the pipe open produces TREE_UNREAPED rather than a false pass. No refusal message echoes an environment value or credential — spawnMessage emits only the OS code, never the path; the hermetic allowlist keeps daemon secrets out of the child to begin with. hermeticVerifierEnvironment is evaluated INSIDE the launch try/catch, so even a hostile non-record base returns a typed SPAWN_FAILED rather than rejecting. ok:true is reachable only when exitCode is non-null AND observedExecutionRejection returns null; TREE_UNREAPED, SPAWN_FAILED, every interruption and EXIT_AMBIGUOUS all return first. Noted, not fixed: capture.stdout.bytes is a Uint8Array that Object.freeze does not deep-freeze — canonical.ts deepFreeze explicitly does not handle typed arrays, so this matches the house convention.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REJECTED: adding new codes to RUNNER_EVIDENCE_ERROR_CODES / a new EVIDENCE_REFUSAL_LAYERS member. evidence-contract.ts is not an owned path and is shared with in-flight work; a frozen closed list is exactly the wrong thing to widen from a neighbouring task. Own list + verbatim pass-through instead.

REJECTED: having the wrapper build the EvidenceReceipt. buildEvidenceReceipt needs resultManifest, graphIdentity, leaseIdentity, effectIdentity and obligations — every one of those is the daemon consumer's fact, not the process wrapper's. The wrapper stops at an ADMISSIBLE ObservedVerifierExecution (gated by the production `observedExecutionRejection`) plus the raw capture. Building a receipt here would be exactly the 'reimplementing receipt authority' DoD 2 forbids.

REJECTED: the wrapper staging declared outputs into the artifact store to synthesize `outputs: ObservedOutput[]`. That is rematerialization/manifest territory and already landed. `outputs` and `runtimeObservation` are caller-supplied inputs; the wrapper owns ONLY the process facts (argv actually spawned, exit, signal, streams, timing).

REJECTED: one single verifier-process.ts. Honest estimate is ~370 physical lines (gate ~60, spawn/capture/reap ~130, classify+assemble ~50, registry ~40, types/codes ~90). Epic rail 5 targets <=250 per FILE. Split into a contract module and a runner module. This is a per-file split, NOT a task split — task-level LOC is explicitly not a bar (project rail).

REJECTED: making every refusal path go through a fake launcher. Timeout, overflow, non-zero exit and ambiguous exit are all forceable with the REAL Node launcher spawning `process.execPath -e '<tiny script>'`, and that is what proves the wrapper on Windows. The counting fake is used only where a real OS cannot be forced deterministically: the invocation-count/duplicate-delivery assertion and TREE_UNREAPED.

CONSIDERED AND KEPT: a pre-spawn `truthClass !== 'PROVEN'` guard that duplicates a rule verifier-execution.ts also enforces post-run. Kept because spawning a child for an observation that can never discharge anything is a real external effect for nothing. It is a conservative EARLIER refusal, never a replacement — the authoritative EXECUTION-layer check still runs after. The two are told apart by layer, which is precisely what epic rail 6 asks the tests to pin.

MEASURED ON DISK 2026-08-09, not read off the description.

(1) GAP CONFIRMED PRESENT. `ls packages/runner/src/evidence/` -> candidate-reconciliation, candidate-rematerialization, evidence-contract, evidence-receipt, receipt-obligations, verification-recipe, verifier-execution. NO verifier-process.*. `grep -rn 'child_process|spawn\(|execFile' packages/*/src --include=*.ts | grep -v .test.ts` -> only packages/runner/src/scope/scope-git.ts and packages/testkit/src/phase0-node-git.ts. Nothing in the repo spawns a verifier. The wrapper is genuinely absent.

(2) BOTH SIDES CONFIRMED ALREADY PRESENT. verifier-execution.ts:1-240 documents itself as 'an OBSERVATION PORT, never a spawn' and exports `observedExecutionRejection(execution, recipe)` + `ObservedVerifierExecution` + `EXECUTION_DISPOSITIONS` (COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED/UNKNOWN). evidence-receipt.ts exports `buildEvidenceReceipt` taking recipe+execution+inputManifest+resultManifest+graph/lease/effect identity+obligations. surface/evidence-surface.ts (70 lines) already publishes both, and index.ts does `export * from './surface/evidence-surface.js'`, so anything added to the surface reaches the @moe/runner root automatically.

(3) ACTIVATION SEAM PRESENT AND ROOT-EXPORTED. supervisor/effect-grant.ts exports `consumeActivationGrant`, `validateActivationCommit`, `initialGrantBinding`, `activationDigestInput`, `deriveGrantId`; effect-activation.ts exports `activateEffect` returning `ActivationCommit {intent, attempt, grant, activationDigest}`. All are in index.ts. effect-grant.ts's own header states the honest limit: 'Handed the same stale UNUSED record twice it consumes it twice, because a pure function has no memory of the first call. Replay is refused by the caller's compare-and-set... and the OS-exclusive launch lock.' THIS WRAPPER IS THAT CALLER. The run registry in step 4 is the memory the pure grant cannot have.

(4) CODE/LAYER LISTS ARE CLOSED AND NOT OWNED BY THIS TASK. `RUNNER_EVIDENCE_ERROR_CODES` and `EVIDENCE_REFUSAL_LAYERS` live in evidence/evidence-contract.ts, which is NOT an owned path. So the wrapper MUST define its own frozen `VERIFIER_PROCESS_ERROR_CODES` + `VERIFIER_PROCESS_LAYERS` and pass foreign failures through VERBATIM rather than re-coding them. That is why the result union carries `source: 'PROCESS'|'SUPERVISOR'|'EVIDENCE'` — it is the mechanism that satisfies epic rail 6's 'which layer refused'.

(5) SPAWN PRECEDENT TO COPY. scope/scope-git.ts:36-77 is the house style for an external-effect call: explicit env allowlist built by `hermeticGitEnvironment(base)` (base is a PARAMETER, never an ambient `process.env` read), `shell: false`, `windowsHide: true`, `maxBuffer`, `timeout`, `stdio: ['ignore','pipe','ignore']`, and ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER given its OWN error code because 'a truncated observation is worse than none'. Mirror all of it.

(6) NODE ADAPTER + .js SHIM CONVENTION. `cat packages/runner/src/evidence/verifier-execution.js` -> exactly one line: `export * from "./verifier-execution.ts";`. Every new .ts needs that sibling. Package is type:module, exports map is `".": "./src/index.ts"`, node engines `>=24.16.0 <25`, tsconfig.base has `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUnusedLocals`. Named Node factories follow `createNodeArtifactFs` / `createNodeGitObserver`.

(7) PLAIN-NODE SMOKE PATTERN EXISTS. runtime-entrypoint.test.ts:26-32 runs `execFile(process.execPath, ['--experimental-strip-types','--input-type=module','-e', src], {cwd: PACKAGE_ROOT})` and imports the BARE specifier `@moe/runner` so Node's self-reference rule goes through the exports map. Its header explains why: 'vitest resolves a ./foo.js specifier back to foo.ts; Node does not'. Copy that probe helper into verifier-process.test.ts — runtime-entrypoint.test.ts is NOT an owned path, do not edit it.

(8) DIGEST HELPERS. canonical.ts exports `sha256Hex(bytes: Uint8Array)` for stream digests and `canonicalDigest(value)` for records, plus `isCanonicalUtcTimestamp`. `ObservedVerifierExecution.startedAt/completedAt` must be canonical UTC or verifier-execution refuses with RUNNER_EVIDENCE_TIMESTAMP_INVALID at layer EXECUTION.
planningNotes.risks:
WINDOWS .cmd/.bat WITH shell:false. Node 24 refuses to spawn a .bat/.cmd/.ps1 without a shell (EINVAL) — and taking the shell is forbidden by task rail 4. Do not let that surface as an opaque spawn error: guard the executable extension in the launch gate and refuse VERIFIER_PROCESS_EXECUTABLE_UNSUPPORTED before any child starts. A recipe must name a real executable (node.exe, git.exe), never a shim.

WINDOWS PROCESS TREE. `child.kill()` on win32 kills only the direct child; grandchildren survive and hold the sealed candidate tree open. Use `execFile('taskkill', ['/pid', String(pid), '/t', '/f'])` on win32 and `detached:true` + `process.kill(-pid, 'SIGKILL')` on posix. After EITHER, you must still AWAIT the 'close' event — kill is a request, reaping is the proof. If close does not arrive inside a bounded reap grace window, that is VERIFIER_PROCESS_TREE_UNREAPED, not success.

EMPTY ENV BREAKS WINDOWS. Stripping env down to nothing makes most Windows executables fail in ways that look like verifier failures. The allowlist must keep SystemRoot, PATH, PATHEXT, COMSPEC, TEMP, TMP, USERPROFILE/HOME, plus LC_ALL=C. Base env is a parameter, never an ambient process.env read (scope-git.ts precedent).

OVERFLOW IS NOT A PASS. Concatenating chunks unbounded is a memory DoS from a chatty verifier. Count bytes as chunks arrive; the moment either stream crosses MAX_VERIFIER_OUTPUT_BYTES, kill the tree and refuse VERIFIER_PROCESS_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW carrying the truncated capture with truncated:true. A truncated capture must never be reported as complete evidence.

RACE: exit before drain. 'exit' can fire before the stdout/stderr pipes have flushed. Resolve on 'close', not 'exit', or the last bytes of evidence are silently lost.

LEAKS ON EVERY EXIT PATH. clearTimeout the deadline timer, remove the abort listener, and detach stream listeners on the refusal paths too — not just the happy one. A retained AbortSignal listener across many runs is an unbounded leak.

AMBIGUOUS EXIT. exitCode null AND signal null, or termination by a signal this wrapper did not send, is not a failure — it is an absence of a fact. It gets VERIFIER_PROCESS_EXIT_AMBIGUOUS and never becomes an ObservedVerifierExecution. This is the concrete shape of epic rail 4's 'unverifiable evidence stays UNKNOWN'.

REGISTRY MUST NOT LEAK OR OVER-REFUSE. Key the map on grant.grantId. In-flight replay ADOPTS the same promise (invocation count stays 1). Post-settlement replay REFUSES with the supervisor's own GRANT_ALREADY_CONSUMED at layer GRANT. Settled entries must be retained (that IS the one-use memory) but store only the settled marker, never the captured bytes, or the map grows without bound.

SHARED WORKTREE (epic rails 2/3). All agents share D:/projexts/moe-next. Commit by explicit pathspec only. Attribute repo-wide gate red by path against the merge-base before treating it as yours. Use `wc -l` for the per-file line check — PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` skips blank lines and will tell you a full file has room.
